historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.5% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue (4.1%) and EPS (11.9%): book value is flat because ~$1.5bn/yr is returned via buybacks and dividends, not because the business shrank. Equity CAGR rejected as the anchor; revenue 5y CAGR selected.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (continuing-ops FCF less SBC incl. equity taxes; interest income not stripped as the company carries net debt): FY2023 ~$1,132M, FY2024 ~$1,616M, FY2025 $2,765M; FY2022 ~$200M (reported $267M) and FY2020 ~$1,520M. The 3y FCF CAGR (FY22-25, ~140%) is set null because it starts from a working-capital trough and is meaningless; 5y FY20-25 ~12.7% is flattered by FY2025's strong receivables collection. Owner-FCF conversion of Operating EBITDA has swung 8%-72% over FY22-25 -- the forward build uses components, not any single year. SBC (~0.5% of revenue) is small, so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are essentially identical. EPS is GAAP and noisy (significant items every year; FY2018-19 loss years around the DowDuPont separation).

scenario_narratives.base: Corteva lands its raised FY2026 guide (Operating EBITDA ~$4.2B) and separates cleanly on 1 Oct. The combined businesses then grow revenue 4-4.5% a year: Seed on Enlist E3 share gains, the out-licensing flywheel (~$1B incremental revenue over a decade) and North American price; Crop Protection on new actives approaching $2B and biologicals toward $1B, while Latin American off-patent herbicides keep losing price to Chinese and Indian generics. Margin gains from mix and productivity (+200bps in H1-26) continue but slow, and roughly $70M a year of two-company overhead is absorbed. Owner-FCF conversion stays constrained by the Latin American receivables book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Separation proves a catalyst for operations, not just multiples: Vylor's pure-play focus accelerates gene editing, hybrid wheat and licensing royalties (high-margin, capital-light), and New Corteva's specialty-chemistry pipeline (7 new actives over the decade) outruns generic erosion. Brazil pricing troughs in 2026 and farm incomes recover with corn/soy prices. Revenue grows 6%+ for three years and Operating EBITDA margin reaches ~27.5% (26.5% after leakage), close to the best-in-class seed and specialty-chem peers.
scenario_narratives.bear: Separation dis-synergies and stranded costs run above plan (~$200M/yr), the Brazil generic price war spreads to North American pre-emergent herbicides, and a farm-income downturn (low corn/soy prices, high rates) pushes growers to trade down on seed and chemistry. FY2027 revenue barely grows and Operating EBITDA margin falls back toward the FY2024 level (~20%), with working capital absorbing more cash as Latin American credit terms stretch. A product-liability or patent loss (paraquat-style claims, Bayer trait litigation) is a further tail not explicitly modelled.
scenario_narratives.separation_note: The 1 Oct 2026 spin is a change of wrapper, not of cash flows: pro-rata distribution means a CTVA holder today owns both halves afterwards. This DCF values the combined claim. The spin's value effect enters through (1) one-off separation costs in the bridge, (2) standalone dis-synergy in the margin paths (0.4pp base, ~1pp bear), and (3) any re-rating of the halves -- which is a market-multiple event, deliberately NOT modelled as intrinsic value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on the combined Corteva (Seed + Crop Protection) as it trades on 25 Sep 2026, with the stock still carrying the Vylor distribution. The imminent 1 Oct 2026 separation is treated as a catalyst and an execution risk, not a source of intrinsic value: a pro-rata spin redistributes the same cash flows between two tickers. It costs real money (one-off separation spend in the bridge, standalone dis-synergy in the margins) and can only create value intrinsically through better operating focus (bull case). Any 'sum of the parts re-rating' is a multiples bet the model deliberately excludes. Operating EBITDA is haircut for Corteva's perennial 'significant items', and legacy pension and environmental liabilities are deducted, because both are real cash the adjusted metrics leave out.
valuation_philosophy.post_separation_instruction: From 1 Oct 2026 the CTVA price excludes Vylor. Compare weighted_iv to (CTVA price + VYLR price) per original CTVA share (1:1 distribution), or rebuild as two separate DCFs once each company files standalone financials (Form 10 carve-out statements for Vylor; New Corteva's recast segment history).
key_risks_to_valuation: Separation execution: stranded costs, dis-synergies above the modelled 0.4pp, new debt at both entities (S&P A-/Moody's Baa1 both on watch negative); the ~$3B facility being arranged around the spin could move leverage between the halves (value-neutral for the combined holder, not for either stub).
Brazil/Latin America generic crop-protection pricing: management does not forecast a 2026 recovery; the bear case assumes it spreads.
Cash conversion: Operating EBITDA to owner FCF has ranged from 8% to 72% (FY22-FY25) on Latin American receivables; the -25% working-capital capture is a judgment.

Legacy liabilities: environmental accrual ($580M), pension ($1.3bn after the H1-26 contribution), and PFAS/paraquat-style litigation beyond the accrual, allocated between Vylor and New Corteva by the separation agreement.
Terminal value: cap multiple binds (15x base) -- valuation is sensitive to the exit multiple for a business the market has priced at 20x+ forward earnings.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 667.196M common shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (24 Jul 2026) plus 1.2M incremental shares from equity plans (Q2-2026 dilutive-securities line). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would charge it twice. Corteva is a repurchaser ($1,071M FY2025, $500M H1-2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 18: stock-based compensation cost $78M (FY24 $64M, FY23 $54M). No combined figure is published and the withholding line is not tagged separately; equity-award tax withholding estimated at ~$23M as SBC ($78M) less the net APIC credit for share-based compensation ($55M, XBRL AdjustmentsToAdditionalPaidInCapitalSharebasedCompensationRequisiteServicePeriodRecognitionValue). SBC incl. equity taxes = $101M.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:03:30Z regular close (Friday). CTVA trades regular-way WITH the Vylor entitlement until the 1 Oct 2026 distribution; VYLR WI when-issued trading began 25 Sep.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.3%, beta ~0.85 (defensive ag-inputs), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~8.5%; debt is ~9% of EV at ~4.5% pre-tax (A-/Baa1, watch negative) -> WACC ~8.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios: separation and Brazil risk are charged in the bear driver paths and the 25% bear weight, not a stacked premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (liability $415M, payments $166M/yr): lease cost sits inside Operating EBITDA and therefore inside the flows; lease liabilities NOT added to net debt. One treatment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest ($244M book, ~$11M/yr of income) deducted in the equity bridge at book; flows are consolidated. Immaterial either way.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing: operating company, moderately cyclical ag-inputs; US filer so no currency/SBC-zero adaptations). No prior DCF and no MEMORY entry -- fresh build. The Oct-1-2026 separation (Vylor = Seed spun 1:1 pro-rata; New Corteva = Crop Protection, keeps ticker) does not change the owner-FCF frame: this values the COMBINED claim the current CTVA price represents (record date 24 Sep passed; shares trade with the Vylor due-bill until 1 Oct). AFTER 1 Oct compare this weighted IV with CTVA + VYLR combined, never with the ex-distribution CTVA price alone. EBITDA path = company Operating EBITDA less ~1.0pp of recurring cash leakage (restructuring 'significant items' recur every year: $579M/$315M/$658M FY23-25, largely non-cash but ~$150-200M cash), and less ~0.4pp standalone dis-synergy from FY2027 (two boards, two listings, two treasuries). FY2026 anchored on raised guidance: Operating EBITDA $4.1-4.3B on revenue ~ $17.9B (H1 +3.8%, Q2 -1%) -> ~23.4% Operating, 22.4% after leakage. Cash tax 27% on EBIT-after-D&A, calibrated to cash taxes paid of $750M FY25 / $707M FY24 against Operating EBITDA less D&A (28%/33%): much of D&A is non-deductible DowDuPont-era intangible amortization. D&A glides 6.8% -> 4.5% as that amortization runs off; capex 3.4% -> 4.0% (standalone footprint). Working capital: receivables + inventory dominate (Latin America credit terms), so growth consumes cash -- wc_capture -25%. BALANCE SHEET: net debt from the 30 Jun 2026 10-Q ($4,875M debt incl. $3,193M short-term, $2,365M cash), which is the seasonal peak; see equity_bridge for the H1 working-capital reversal and the debt-like items (pension, environmental, NCI, separation costs). Cross-check on the 31 Dec 2025 balance sheet (net cash $1,950M less H1 buybacks $500M, dividends $241M and the $1,140M pension contribution, then the same debt-like items) gives -$2.0bn of bridge vs -$2.2bn here.

base.narrative: Guided FY2026, then mid-single-digit growth from new crop-protection actives, biologicals and Enlist licensing, partly offset by Brazil generic pricing; Operating EBITDA margin creeps to ~25% (24% after leakage) net of standalone dis-synergy.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: a live two-way separation with new capital structures, new CEOs and ratings on watch negative, plus unresolved Brazil generic pricing, makes the downside path materially more likely than for a steady-state compounder. Base at 50% because FY2026 guidance was raised and H1 delivered it. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once -- Brazil troughing, farm-income recovery and post-spin execution in both companies.
